title: Courtyard Fountain Designer with Undo/Redo
description: The user designs an architectural courtyard fountain by placing Duck statues and WaterBottle pillars on a circular stone platform. Ducks act as decorative water-spout sculptures and WaterBottles serve as structural column elements. A water budget conservation law limits total placed objects to 8, and repositioning or swapping elements requires multi-input coupling between rotation, height, and radial distance sliders.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap with ES modules from cdn.jsdelivr.net). Load Duck.glb and WaterBottle.glb via GLTFLoader from 'shared_assets/'. Scene setup: a circular stone-textured platform (radius 5, MeshStandardMaterial with gray color and roughness 0.8) centered at origin. Add a hemisphere light (sky 0x87CEEB, ground 0x444444, intensity 1) and a directional light casting shadows. Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (8,6,8) looking at origin, with OrbitControls. Interaction system (10-14 steps expected): 1) A toolbar with two buttons: 'Place Duck Spout' and 'Place Bottle Pillar'. Clicking a button enters placement mode. 2) Clicking on the platform places a clone of the respective GLB at that position. Scale Duck to 1.5x and WaterBottle to 3x for architectural proportion. 3) Conservation law: a 'Water Budget' counter starts at 8. Each Duck costs 2 units, each WaterBottle costs 1 unit. Display remaining budget in a HUD. Placement is blocked when budget is insufficient. 4) Selecting a placed object (raycaster click) opens a coupled parameter panel with three sliders: radial distance from center (1-4.5), angle around center (0-360), and height offset (0-2). Changing radial distance auto-adjusts height using formula: height = 0.3 * radialDistance (multi-input coupling). 5) A 'Swap Type' button converts a selected Duck into a WaterBottle or vice versa, adjusting the budget accordingly (blocked if budget insufficient for the swap). 6) Full undo/redo stack: store each action (place, move, swap, delete) as a command object. Undo button (Ctrl+Z) reverts the last action restoring positions, types, and budget. Redo button (Ctrl+Y) re-applies. Support at least 20 history entries. 7) A 'Delete' button removes the selected object and refunds its budget cost. 8) All placed objects auto-rotate to face the platform center (lookAt origin, then rotate Y by 180 degrees). Style the HUD with a semi-transparent dark panel showing budget, object count, and undo/redo buttons.
